newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia Dec credit rating stays stable at DB3a.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia Dec credit rating stays stable at DB3a.

text.p: Slovenia's credit rating remained stable in December despite an inconclusive result in a general election in November, Dun and Bradstreet's (D&B) Ljubljana representative said on Monday.

"Following the inconclusive result of general elctions held on November 10, it remains unclear whether Slovenia's political stability will remain fully intact," the agency said in its latest Risk & Payment Review.
D&B gave Slovenia for the sixth month in a row an unchanged DB3a credit rating for December, placing it second in the region just behind Czech Republic and ahead of Poland.
The November election gave neither right or left a mandate to run the government. An alliance of right-wing parties failed to win an absolute majority by just one seat.
Acting Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek's centre-left Liberal Democrats remained the biggest party but are struggling to form a new coalition.
"The tolar's continuing strength and wage growth have hurt export competitiveness at a time when economic growth is already slowing," D&B noted.
It estimated the real growth of Slovenia's GDP for 1996 at 3.1 percent.
The latest figures on GDP growth released by the state statistical office last week, showed 1995 real GDP growth at 3.9 percent, down from 4.9 percent in 1994.
